description: Amendment to the National Institute of Language Education and Training Act, No.26 of 2007
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-11-23 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - As per the provisions of the National Institute of Language Education and Training Act No.26 of 2007, the incumbent Secretaries of the Ministries in charge of the subjects of Education, Public Administration, Finance, and Constitutional Affairs and National Integration serve as ex-officio members of the Management Board of the National Institute of Language Education and Training. However, it has been observed that, due to the heavy workload of these officials, practical difficulties arise regarding their participation in the monthly meetings of the Management Board. Therefore, the Cabinet approved proposal made by the Minister of Justice and National Integration to instruct the Legal Draftsman to prepare a Bill to amend the relevant sections of the National Institute of Language Education and Training Act, No.26 of 2007, enabling to make provisions for the appointment of ex-officio members to the said Management Board in a manner that minimizes such difficulties.

description: Construction of a new building complex for the Puttalam District Secretariat
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-11-23 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Although it has been proposed to construct a building complex consisting of three sections for the Puttalam District Secretariat in 2013, only the four-storey building on the southern side has been constructed as of now. Due to insufficient space and inadequate facilities in the said building, divisions of the office have had to be accommodated at different locations, thereby causing a hindrance to the coordination of administrative activities and the direct supervision by the District Secretary. Therefore, construction of a building complex equipped with modern facilities has been identified as a priority requirement, with the objectives of providing proper accommodation for various office divisions, strengthening administrative coordination, facilitating the delivery of public services, and ensuring adequate facilities for district-level meetings and conferences. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Public Administration, Provincial Councils and Local Government to construct a new building complex for the Puttalam District Secretariat comprising a four-storey office building, an auditorium with a seating capacity of 1,000, and a parking area within the premises where the existing office is currently located, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of a Six-Storey Building for the Base Hospital, Puttalam
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-11-23 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval was granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2026-03-03 to transfer the Base Hospital, Puttalam which was under the purview of the North Western Provincial Council, to the Central Government with the concurrence of the Governor of the North Western Province with a view to developing and upgrading the same. It has been found essential to develop and enhance the infrastructure of the said hospital to ensure the provision of quality and continuous medical services to patients by the hospital. Accordingly, it has been planned to construct a six- storey building with a total floor area of ​​8,640 square meters for the Base Hospital, Puttalam over a period of 04 years, which can accommodate the Accident and Emergency Care Unit, Clinics, Short-Stay Unit, Blood Bank as well as Diagnostic and Laboratory Facilities. The Government of India has agreed to provide a Grant of Rs. 600 million for the construction of the first three floors of the proposed building where the Accident and Emergency Care Unit is intended to be established. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Health and Mass Media to implement the project for the construction of the proposed six-storey building at the Base Hospital, Puttalam and to enter into the Memorandum of Understanding with the Government of India to secure a Grant of Rs.600 million for the construction of its first three floors, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on Cooperation in Capacity Building between His Majesty’s Revenue and Customs of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland and the Sri Lanka Customs
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-11-23 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - His Majesty’s Revenue and Customs of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland has proposed entering into a Memorandum of Understanding on Cooperation in Capacity Building with Sri Lanka Customs with the objective of establishing a framework for capacity building and technical assistance in relation to the implementation of the World Trade Organization’s Trade Facilitation Agreement. Through the proposed MoU, it is intended to support Sri Lanka Customs in customs and trade facilitation reforms via technical cooperation, capacity building, workshops, technical advice, knowledge exchange and opportunities for learning visits. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President, in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development, to enter into the proposed Memorandum of Understanding on Cooperation in Capacity Building, between His Majesty’s Revenue and Customs of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland and Sri Lanka Customs, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Obtaining assistance of the OPEC Fund for International Development for the implementation of the Sri Lanka Reform for Growth, Resilience and Openness Development Policy Operation
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-11-23 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Government of Sri Lanka is implementing a comprehensive programme of economic stabilization, recovery and structural reforms aimed at restoring macroeconomic stability, ensuring fiscal sustainability and laying the foundation for sustainable and inclusive economic growth. Following a positive assessment of the said reform programme and policy commitments, the OPEC Fund for International Development has agreed to grant a Policy-Based Loan of USD 30 million. The said Loan Facility is to be provided in parallel with financial assistance provided by the World Bank under the Development Policy Operation. The proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning, and Economic Development to obtain the said loan consisting of USD 24 million under Ordinary Capital Resources and USD 6 million under Special Capital Resources from the OPEC Fund for International Development, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Increasing the number of beneficiaries and the Capital Financial Grant of the Social Protection Project implemented under the World Bank Loan Programme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-11-16 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Cabinet, at its meeting held on 2025-10-13, granted approval to implement the programme for empowering poor and extremely poor families receiving benefits under the Aswesuma Scheme, under the financial assistance of the Asian Development Bank and the World Bank. The programme implemented by the Asian Development Bank has now been concluded, having provided the relevant capital financial grants to 8,660 families under the financial assistance of the said Bank. Capital financial grants have been provided to 4,900 families across 07 Districts at the first phase by the programme implemented under the Social Protection Project of the World Bank Loan Programme and at the second phase, plans are in place to provide capital financial grants to 6,600 families identified in 05 Districts by now. Based on the experience gained during the implementation of the first phase of the Social Protection Project, the World Bank has agreed to increase the financial grant provided to each family unit of empowerment, as well as to expand the number of anticipated beneficiaries of the project, without compromising the quality of the project. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Rural Development, Social Security and Community Empowerment to increase the number of beneficiaries expected to empower under the Social Protection Project of the World Bank Loan Programme from 10,975 to 11,500 and to expand the maximum limit of capital financial grant currently set at Rs.150,000/- to Rs.200,000 for eligible beneficiary families identified under the second phase of the said project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of Stage I of the Oliyamulla Pumping Station Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-11-16 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The canal system associated with the Mudun Ela catchment area connects to the Kelani River at the areas of Oliyamulla, Peliyagoda and Pethiyagoda. During flood periods in the upper reaches of the Kelani River, floodwaters enter the said urban areas through those canals, placing the low-lying areas within the Mudun Ela catchment at risk of flooding. Studies conducted on the said issue have recommended the construction of a water pumping station in the Oliyamulla area where the main canal of the relevant catchment connects to the Kelani River, to mitigate flood risks. Accordingly, it has been planned to implement a project for the construction of water pumping stations with a total capacity of 35m³/s, under the financial assistance of the Government of Sri Lanka and the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA). It is expected to construct a pumping station with a capacity of 15m³/s under stage I and another with a capacity of 20m³/s under stage II, of the relevant project. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development to implement Stage I of the Oliyamulla Pumping Station Project during the period of 2027-2031, under a total estimated cost of Rs.5,962.13 million, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Strengthening meaningful youth participation in environmental processes and environmental education
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-11-16 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - More attention has been focused both nationally and internationally on strengthening youth participation in environmental conservation and sustainable development. A resolution on 'Enhancing Meaningful Youth Participation in Environmental Processes and Environmental Education' presented by Sri Lanka, was adopted at the seventh session of the United Nations Environment Assembly held in Nairobi, Kenya, in December 2025. Accordingly, as a Member State of the United Nations, Sri Lanka along with the international community is committed to implementing the said resolution. Furthermore, to foster meaningful youth participation in environmental education and action, it is possible to get the youth clubs currently established at the Grama Niladhari Division level, the Federation of youth clubs established at the district and national levels, as well as institutions such as the National Youth Services Council and the National Youth Corps involved, in order to implement youth related activities at the grassroots level under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports. Accordingly, the joint proposal made by the Minister of Youth Affairs and Sports; and the Minister of Environment to launch national environmental programmes jointly by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports; and the Ministry of Environment, utilizing the aforementioned mechanism to promote environmental activities to implement these programmes and activities at the regional level; and to establish a National Environmental Steering Committee to ensure the proper execution of the said national environmental programmes at the regional level, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of the National Nuclear Security Coordination Committee
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-11-16 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - As a member state of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA),                        Sri Lanka is committed to maintaining an effective national nuclear security regime to prevent, detect, and respond to unauthorized or criminal acts involving nuclear and other radioactive materials, associated facilities, and related activities. Accordingly, the need has been identified to formally establish a National Committee comprising representatives from institutions responsible for security, legal, and other relevant domains to serve as a permanent, centralized mechanism dedicated to aligning nuclear security policies, assessing threats, and coordinating operations. It has been proposed to establish the said Committee under the Chairmanship of the Secretary, Ministry of Science and Technology, and the Director General of the Sri Lanka Atomic Energy Regulatory Council will function as the Secretary of the said Committee. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Science and Technology to establish the said National Nuclear Security Coordination Committee under the Ministry of Science and Technology, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of the Bangladesh-Sri Lanka Joint Consultative Commission for Comprehensive Cooperation between the Government of Bangladesh and the Government of Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-11-16 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Government of Bangladesh and the Government of Sri Lanka have agreed to sign a Memorandum of Understanding on the Establishment of the Bangladesh-Sri Lanka Joint Consultative Commission for Comprehensive Cooperation between the two parties. The MoU seeks to achieve the objectives such as elevating the existing mechanism of political consultations to the foreign ministerial level effectively reviewing and evaluating all areas of ongoing bilateral cooperation. Clearance of the Attorney General has been received for the draft Memorandum of Understanding. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment, and Tourism to sign the MoU on the establishment of the Bangladesh-Sri Lanka Joint Consultative Commission, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Entering into Memoranda of Understanding/Agreement between Sri Lankan Universities and Foreign Universities for the purpose of Educational Cooperation
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-11-16 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body:
- It has been recognized that establishing higher educational cooperation with foreign universities is essential for elevating Sri Lankan universities in world ranking indicators and internationalization. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister, in her capacity as the Minister of Education, Higher Education, and Vocational Education to enter into the following Memoranda of Understanding/Agreement between universities in Sri Lanka and foreign universities, was approved by the Cabinet:

The Memorandum of Understanding between the University of Colombo of Sri Lanka and the Manipal Academy of Higher Education of India with the objectives of enhancing educational cooperation, exchanging material relating to publications and academic information, exchanging academic staff, research scholars and students and obtaining technical assistance.


The Memorandum of Understanding between the Buddhist and Pali University of Sri Lanka and the Mahamakut Buddhist University of Thailand on Academic and Research Collaboration.


The Memorandum of Understanding among the University of Moratuwa of Sri Lanka, Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University of China and the Universitat La Salle, Barcelona of Spain on Research Collaboration.


The Memorandum of Understanding between the University of Peradeniya of Sri Lanka and the Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology, the Commonwealth of Australia regarding the conduct of collaborative research training programmes, carrying out activities related to submitting publications and research cooperation, and the Umbrella Cotutelle Agreement between the two parties concerning the implementation of collaborative research training programmes and awarding postgraduate study programmes.

description: Establishment of the National Commission on Research and Development and its affiliated Office
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-11-16 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Policy approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2026-06-22 to establish the 'National Commission on Research and Development', recognizing the importance of directing the field of innovation and research towards a novel path to enhance the economic stability and the production capacity. Accordingly, an Expert Committee comprising specialists in the relevant field appointed by the Secretary to the President, has prepared a concept paper to serve as the basis for drafting legal provisions for the establishment of the proposed Commission and its affiliated Office. According to the said concept paper, the National Commission on Research and Development will function as the central body responsible for the strategic direction, coordination, monitoring, and development in research and development system of Sri Lanka. Furthermore, the said concept paper provides recommendations as well for the proposed governance structure, institutional provisions, and implementing procedure, aimed at creating a more efficient national research and development environment. Accordingly, the joint proposal made by the Hon. President and the Minister of Science and Technology to instruct the Legal Draftsman to prepare a Bill for the establishment of the National Commission on Research and Development and its affiliated Office, based on the aforementioned concept paper, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Submission of the Veterinary Surgeons and Practitioners (Infamous Conduct) Regulations, No.1 of 2025, to Parliament for approval
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-11-09 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Veterinary Surgeons and Practitioners Act, No.46 of 1956 was introduced with a view to establishing a legal framework for the registration of veterinary surgeons and practitioners in Sri Lanka, defining their professional qualifications, and establishing the Sri Lanka Veterinary Council to regulate the veterinary profession. The Regulations published through the Gazette Extraordinary Notification No.2470/12 dated 2026-01-05, have been made with the objective of empowering the Sri Lanka Veterinary Council to define professional misconduct including acts or omissions constituting misuse of position falling under the category of 'Infamous Conduct'; establish a mechanism for appointing 'Inquiry Boards' to investigate such conduct; and impose penalties on offenders, including temporary suspension of registration, cancellation of registration and issuance of warnings. Accordingly, the Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Land, and Irrigation to present the 'Veterinary Surgeons and Practitioners (Infamous Conduct) Regulations, No.1 of 2025 so published, to Parliament for approval.

description: Construction of a new railway bridge across the Mahaweli River between Sarasavi Uyana and Peradeniya of the Matale railway line
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-11-09 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - A project has been planned to be implemented to develop an extensive suburban railway network covering the Kandy Municipal Area, and a feasibility study in this regard is currently underway. The scope of the said project includes the construction of a double-track railway line of the main railway line from Kadugannawa to Gampola (via Peradeniya) and double-tracking of the Matale Railway Line from Peradeniya to Katugastota. It has been identified that measures should be taken under the said project to complete the planned double-track railway line, eliminate the existing single-track bottleneck and enhance the reliability and connectivity of the railway network. Accordingly, the Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways, and Urban Development to construct a new railway bridge across the Mahaweli River between Sarasavi Uyana and Peradeniya, obtaining financial assistance from the Indian Line of Credit allocated for the reconstruction and development of railway infrastructure damaged by Cyclone Ditwah, enabling to integrate the Matale railway line with the national railway network.

description: Obtaining financial assistance for the Sector Development Programme (Sub‑programme 1) on Building a Strong and Inclusive Financial Ecosystem for Micro, Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-11-09 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2026-03-16 to conduct loan negotiations with the Asian Development Bank to secure a Policy-Based Loan of USD 620 million structured under five sub‑programmes, in order to advance                   Sri Lanka’s reform agenda in parallel with the International Monetary Fund's Extended Fund Facility programme. As per the said approval, the Department of External Resources has now concluded formal loan negotiations with the Asian Development Bank to obtain the relevant funds for the implementation of Sub‑programme 1 of the  Sector Development Programme on Building a Strong and Inclusive Financial Ecosystem for Micro, Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises. Accordingly, the proposal made by the President, in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development, to enter into an agreement with the Asian Development Bank to obtain the said loan consisting of a Policy‑Based Loan Component of USD 100 million and a Financial Intermediation Loan Component of USD 100 million, funded through the Regular Ordinary Capital Resources of the Asian Development Bank, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Awarding the contract for the construction of a ten-storied building for the Faculty of Commerce and Management Studies of the University of Kelaniya
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-11-09 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2025-02-03 to call for bids by following the national competitive bidding method and select a contractor to implement the project for the construction of a ten‑storied building for the Faculty of Commerce and Management Studies of the University of Kelaniya, which had been halted due to the economic crisis. Accordingly, bids were invited, and ten (10) bids were received. Taking into consideration the recommendations submitted by the High Level Procurement Committee and the Procurement Appeal Board following the evaluation of those bids, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in her capacity as the Minister of Education, Higher Education, and Vocational Education to award the said contract to M/s Sathuta Builders (Pvt) Ltd., substantially responsive lowest evaluated bidder, for a sum of Rs.1.73 billion (excluding Value Added Tax), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementing a 'Home Composting' Project in collaboration with Provincial Councils and Local Authorities as a component of the 'Clean Sri Lanka -Pivithuru Purawara' National Solid Waste Management Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-11-09 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - It has been identified that 50% - 60% of the solid waste generated daily in Sri Lanka consists of biodegradable organic materials and that converting the aforesaid waste into compost at the household level can significantly reduce the financial and operational costs associated with waste collection, transportation, segregation, recycling, and final disposal. Therefore, as a sustainable solution covering the entire waste lifecycle from generation to final disposal, it has been planned to implement a project to convert household generated biodegradable waste into compost under the 'Clean Sri Lanka - Pivithuru Purawara' National Solid Waste Management Project scheduled to be implemented during the period of 2027 ‑ 2029 as one component thereof. Under this project, household compost bins will be provided to the housing units concerned and the process of converting biodegradable waste into compost within the respective household premises will be continued with a view to designating street segments selected by Local Authorities covering all Local Authorities as areas where organic waste collection services are not provided. The intervention seeks to integrate several key components into a single, operational system: the provision of the necessary physical infrastructure to convert waste into compost (compost bins), the transfer of knowledge and technical guidance, supervision by all Local Authorities and the continuous practice of composting at household levels. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President to implement the Home Composting Project initially covering the Western and Southern Provinces as one of the projects of the three-year 'Clean Sri Lanka - Pivithuru Purawara' National Solid Waste Management Project and to expand the project to other Provinces based on its success, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Entering into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the George Mason University of the United States of America and the Arthur C. Clarke Institute for Modern Technologies to promote Research Collaboration in the field of Science and Technology
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-11-09 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - It has been proposed to sign a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between George Mason University in the United States of America and the Arthur C. Clarke Institute for Modern Technologies in Sri Lanka with the objective of facilitating a mutually beneficial research collaboration, including the identification of research challenges and the development of technical solutions between the two parties. Under the said MoU, which will be effective for a period of five (05) years, both parties have agreed to collaborate in the areas of cybersecurity, unmanned aerial vehicles, space and satellites, artificial intelligence and machine learning and 5G communications. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Science and Technology to sign the proposed Memorandum of Understanding between the George Mason University of the United States of America and the Arthur C. Clarke Institute for Modern Technologies in Sri Lanka, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Entering into a Memorandum of Understanding between Sri Lanka and India for the supply of new 100 Ambulances to the 1990 Suwaseriya National Emergency Ambulance Service
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-11-09 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The '1990 Suwaseriya National Emergency Ambulance Service' was launched in 2016 with the support of a Financial Grant from the Government of India and was expanded island-wide in the year 2018. The said Service provides a free 24‑hour service covering all Districts and handles between 1,000 - 1,200 patient transport requests daily. These Ambulances run approximately 9 million kilometers annually, thereby increasing the likelihood of mechanical breakdowns arising within the current fleet of 322 Ambulances. The Government of India has agreed to provide a Financial Grant, enabling to procure 100 new, fully medically equipped ambulances for use by the 1990 Suwaseriya Service, taking into account a special request made by the Government of Sri Lanka. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Health and Mass Media to enter into a Memorandum of Understanding with the Government of India for the purpose of obtaining the said Financial Grant, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Entering into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the University of Jaffna, Sri Lanka, and the Board of Trustees of Southern Illinois University of the United States of America
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-11-09 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - It has been proposed to sign a Memorandum of Understanding between the University of Jaffna and the Board of Trustees of Southern Illinois University of the United States of America, with the objective of further strengthening the friendly relations between the two Countries by working towards achieving excellence in academic activities and advancing and disseminating knowledge. By entering into the proposed MoU, it is expected to foster collaboration in several areas such as engaging in joint research and educational activities, promoting international experience through the exchange of academic staff for research, lectures and discussions in all fields of study, encouraging the exchange of undergraduate and postgraduate students for learning, research, and internships, organizing joint symposiums, conferences and seminars and facilitating the exchange of information by linking the websites of the said two Universities. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in her capacity as the Minister of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education, to sign the proposed Memorandum of Understanding between the University of Jaffna, Sri Lanka, and the Board of Trustees of Southern Illinois University of the United States of America to be effective for a period of five (05) years from the date of signing, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Recommendations submitted by the Finance Commission for the year 2027
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-11-09 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - In accordance with the provisions of Article 154 of the Constitution, the Finance Commission is mandated to make recommendations regarding the resources required for the Provincial Councils established as per the 13th Amendment to the Constitution as well as the principles to be followed in allocating grants from the National Budget to each Provincial Council. Accordingly, with the objective of achieving a balanced regional development across the Country, the Finance Commission has submitted its recommendations to the President pertaining to the policies to be followed in distributing funds among Provincial Councils, which are allocated to Provincial Councils from the Annual Budget 2027, as well as the Government interventions required for more efficient delivery of services related to the subjects assigned to the Provincial Councils. The proposal submitted by the President to implement the said recommendations and to submit the same to Parliament, in accordance with the provisions of paragraph (7) of Article 154R of the Constitution, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Making provisions to give effect to the Sri Lanka's obligations under the Convention on Cluster Munitions
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-11-02 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Sri Lanka signed the Convention on Cluster Munitions (Oslo Convention) on 2018 02 28. Approval was granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2019 03 19, to draft necessary legislation to give effect to the obligations under the said Convention in the country. Accordingly, the Cluster Munitions Prohibition Preliminary Bill prepared by the Legal Draftsman has been updated incorporating amendments proposed on several occasions. The proposal made by the President, in his capacity as the Minister of Defence, to grant policy approval for drafting the Cluster Munitions Prohibition Bill by incorporating new amendments identified by now to incorporate to the said Bill, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Augmentation of Kolonnawa Grid Substation for the Development of 100 MW/100 MWh Battery Energy Storage System
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-11-02 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - It has been planned to establish Sri Lanka’s first utility-scale Battery Energy Storage System at the Kolonnawa Grid Substation in alignment with the Long Term Power Generation Expansion Plans.  Accordingly, approval was granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2024 09 02, to upgrade the Kolonnawa Grid Substation for the development of 100 MW/100 MWh Battery Energy Storage Systems under the Power System Strengthening and Renewable Energy Integration Project, by utilizing the funds of the Asian Development Bank. Bids have been invited following the international competitive procurement method to select a contractor for the implementation of the said project and four bids have been received for the same. The proposal made by the Minister of Energy to award the said contract to Joint Venture of Ceylex Engineering (Pvt.) Ltd and Xingneng Electric Power Construction Co. description: Land Development and Drainage System Improvement Project related to the Rathgama Town Development Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-11-02 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body:
- Due to the absence of a properly designed drainage system in the surrounding areas of the Rathgama Town, a service town located between the Galle and Hikkaduwa with tourist attraction in the Southern Province, roads and surrounding areas are frequently inundated several times a year. To address this issue, the Urban Development Authority has planned to implement a project for the development of the new Rathgama town. The Cabinet approved a proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways, and Urban Development to implement the relevant Land Development and Drainage System Improvement Project in accordance with the plans of the said Town Development Project through the Sri Lanka Land Development Corporation at an estimated cost of Rs. 3,380.22 million (inclusive of Value Added Tax), during the period of 2027 2029 with the following components:

* Creation of a water pond and water retention areas within a land area of approximately 13 acres of approximately 24.5-acre paddy land (abandoned) which has been acquired by the Sri Lanka Land Development Corporation situated between Rathgama Dodangoda Road and Wijerathna Road, and development of the remaining portions of the land. 

* Development of the canal banks, construction of the maintenance access road, improvement of the drainage system and development of the remaining land portions by acquiring approximately 1.5 acres in the lower section of the 24.5-acre said paddy land to ensure the proper diversion of excess rainwater into the Rathgama Lagoon.
